scope: Panhandle & South Plains (Lubbock, Potter, Randall counties; Lubbock, Amarillo)

records.name: South Plains Food Bank Food Assistance
records.description_en: The food bank gives food to people in need in Lubbock and the South Plains. You fill out a food help form and pick up a food voucher.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in the South Plains who need food. The website does not list income limits.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the Food Assistance Form online, or call. If you need food right away, call 2-1-1.
records.hours: Applications Mon-Thu 8:30am-5:00pm. Voucher pickup: Mon, Tue, Thu 8:30am-11:45am and 12:30pm-5:30pm; Wed and Fri 8:30am-11:45am.
records.notes: Serves 19 South Plains counties. Application status questions: text or call (806) 642-6724. Also has a zip-code map of partner pantries on the Need Food page.

records.name: Senior Box Program (CSFP)
records.description_en: A free monthly box of USDA food for older adults with low income.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For seniors age 60 or older who meet income rules.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the Senior Box referral form online or call the food bank.
records.notes: Commodity Supplemental Food Program run with the Texas Department of Agriculture. Income limits not listed on the page.

records.name: Mobile Pantry
records.description_en: A food truck brings free food to towns across the South Plains on set days each month.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people who need food in the counties the food bank serves. No income limits are listed.
records.how_to_apply: Check the monthly Mobile Pantry calendar online for a site and date near you, or call the food bank.
records.notes: Calendar is updated monthly; times vary by site (often 10am-2pm). Confirm Lubbock County sites on the calendar.

records.name: Lubbock Meals on Wheels
records.description_en: Volunteers bring healthy meals to the homes of people who cannot easily leave home. They also offer a weekend meal program.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in the Lubbock area who are homebound, elderly, or disabled.
records.how_to_apply: Call Lubbock Meals on Wheels to ask about signing up.
records.notes: Also serves people with disabilities who are homebound, not only seniors. Not government or United Way funded.

records.name: Comprehensive Energy Assistance Program (CEAP) - Lubbock County
records.description_en: Helps pay electric, gas, and propane bills for low-income homes in Lubbock County. Also offers food vouchers and emergency help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Household income must be below 150% of the federal poverty guidelines.
records.how_to_apply: Call Neighborhood House to ask about applying for energy help.
records.notes: City of Lubbock Utilities lists Neighborhood House as the CEAP provider. Address and hours come from Upbring's Neighborhood House page (https://www.upbring.org/programs-and-services/community-services/neighborhood-house/), which may be older - call to confirm.

records.name: Lubbock County General Assistance (LCGA)
records.description_en: Gives short-term money help to Lubbock County families, such as help with the current month's utility bill.
records.eligibility_summary_en: The household must include a disabled adult or a child, have had no income for at least 30 days, and have lived in the county at least 30 days. Head of household must be 18 or older.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Lubbock County resident for at least 30 days

records.how_to_apply: Call Lubbock County General Assistance.
records.notes: Limited to the current month only; deposits and past-due bills are not covered.

records.name: Direct Client Assistance Program
records.description_en: Helps adults and seniors with utility bills, food, hygiene items, eye exams, glasses, and prescriptions.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For adults and seniors in need. The City of Lubbock says they have no income requirement for utility help.
documents_needed: ID for all adults in the household
Social Security cards for everyone in the household
Proof of income for the last 30 days
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the online form (Apply Now / Registrar Ahora) or call. They answer within 2 business days.
records.notes: They limit how many forms they accept each week. Seniors 60+ may also get dental, prescription, and hearing aid help.

records.name: The Salvation Army Lubbock
records.organization: The Salvation Army Texas South Plains
records.description_en: Offers shelter and other help in Lubbock, including a one-time utility payment of up to $150 per year.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in need in the Lubbock area.
records.how_to_apply: Call or visit The Salvation Army in Lubbock.
records.notes: $150-per-year utility help is listed on the City of Lubbock Utility Assistance page (https://www.mylubbock.us/645/Utility-Assistance). Shelter hours not listed online.

records.name: Public Housing and Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8)
records.organization: Housing Authority of the City of Lubbock
records.description_en: Offers low-rent public housing and vouchers that help pay rent in private homes in Lubbock.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income households. Voucher income generally cannot exceed 50% of area median income. Must be a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Housing Authority's application portal, where you can also check your waiting list status.
records.notes: Also offers Project Based Vouchers and a Mainstream Voucher Program. Waiting list status not shown on page.

records.name: City of Lubbock Community Development
records.description_en: Uses federal and state grants for housing repair, energy help and HVAC repairs, and services for people who are homeless or low-income.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income households, people who are homeless or at risk, and elderly or disabled people in Lubbock.
records.how_to_apply: Call or visit the Community Development office to ask what programs are open.
records.notes: Page does not list specific open programs or eligibility; call first.

records.name: ECHO West Texas - Homeless Coordinated Entry
records.description_en: Lubbock's lead agency for homeless services. It connects people who are homeless to housing and other help.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Lubbock who are homeless or about to lose housing.
records.how_to_apply: Call ECHO West Texas to ask about coordinated entry.
records.notes: Lubbock's designated Continuum of Care lead agency. Hours not listed.

records.name: Open Door Community Center and Supportive Housing
records.description_en: A day center for people experiencing homelessness in Lubbock. Open Door also runs supportive housing and housing for survivors.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Lubbock who are homeless or were homeless.
records.how_to_apply: Walk in to the Community Center during open hours or call.
records.notes: Admin office is at 1918 13th St.

records.name: StarCare Specialty Health System (Local Mental Health Authority)
records.description_en: Lubbock's public mental health center. Offers crisis help, counseling, medicine, substance use treatment, and services for people with intellectual disabilities.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in the Lubbock area with mental health, substance use, or intellectual disability needs. Anyone in crisis can call 24/7.
records.how_to_apply: In a crisis call (806) 740-1414. For services, call intake at (806) 740-1421.
records.notes: Crisis line (806) 740-1414 or toll-free (800) 687-7581. Sunrise Canyon Hospital: 1950 Aspen Ave, (806) 740-1420.

records.name: VetStar Veteran Services
records.description_en: Helps veterans and their families with peer support and one-time help with rent, mortgage, utilities, food, and rides.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For service members, veterans, and their families. City of Lubbock says utility help requires income at or below 80% of area median income and proof of veteran status.
records.how_to_apply: Call VetStar.
records.notes: Utility help details from https://www.mylubbock.us/645/Utility-Assistance. Financial help is through the Texas Veterans Commission GAP grant.

records.name: Community Health Center of Lubbock
records.organization: The Community Health Center of Lubbock, Inc.
records.description_en: A federally funded health center with medical, dental, eye, behavioral health, pharmacy, and pediatric care.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone, including people without insurance.
records.how_to_apply: Call to make an appointment. Same-day care and telehealth are offered.
records.notes: Several clinic sites: 96 West, Arnett Benson, Chatman, Community Dental, Medical Office Plaza, Parkway, West. Sliding fee not stated on the page.

records.name: Lubbock Public Health Clinical Services
records.description_en: Low-cost vaccines for children and adults, and testing and treatment for sexually transmitted infections.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the public. Help is available for people who cannot pay.
records.how_to_apply: Call or come during walk-in hours for STI testing.
records.hours: Office Mon-Thu 8am-5pm, Fri 8am-noon. STI walk-in: Tue all day, Wed AM, Thu PM, Fri AM.
records.cost: Child vaccines $13 first dose, $7 each additional; adult vaccines $20; financial assistance available

records.name: Workforce Solutions South Plains - Lubbock Career Center
records.description_en: Free help finding a job, job readiness workshops, and job training.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to job seekers in the South Plains.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the Lubbock Career Center or call.

records.name: Child Care Services (CCS) - South Plains
records.description_en: Helps working families and students pay for child care.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Family income at or below 85% of state median income. Single parents must work or go to school about 25 hours a week (50 combined for two parents).

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Resident of Bailey, Cochran, Crosby, Dickens, Floyd, Garza, Hale, Hockley, King, Lamb, Lubbock, Lynn, Motley, Terry, or Yoakum County

records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Texas Workforce Commission child care portal.
records.notes: Enrollment was listed as CLOSED with a waitlist averaging about 15 months. Email childcareservices@spworkforce.org.

records.name: CitiAccess Paratransit
records.description_en: Door-to-door bus rides in Lubbock for people with disabilities who are approved for CitiAccess.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For riders approved for CitiAccess (people with disabilities).
records.how_to_apply: Approved riders call Citibus customer service to book a ride.
records.notes: The OnDemand app is no longer used for booking CitiAccess rides. Fare and application details not on the page.

records.name: South Plains Area Agency on Aging
records.description_en: Helps older adults with benefits counseling, caregiver support, nursing home advocacy, and care coordination such as medical equipment, home repairs, and transportation.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people age 60 or older, their caregivers, and anyone eligible for Medicare.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Information & Assistance line.
records.notes: Toll-free (888) 418-6564. SPAG main line (806) 762-8721.

records.name: High Plains Food Bank Food Assistance
records.description_en: The regional food bank for the Texas Panhandle. It refers people to more than 140 partner pantries and runs food programs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in the Texas Panhandle who need food.
records.how_to_apply: Call or fill out the help form on the Get Help page. Staff can refer you to a nearby pantry.
records.notes: Serves 29 Panhandle counties. Also helps people apply for SNAP, CHIP, Medicaid, and TANF. Kids Cafe at 2199 SE 8th Ave.

records.name: Senior Adult Food Program (CSFP)
records.description_en: A free monthly box of food for older adults with low income.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For seniors age 60 or older who meet USDA income guidelines. You can self-declare your income.
records.how_to_apply: Sign up at a distribution site, download the application online, or call.
records.notes: Proof of income is not required.

records.name: InterFaith Hunger Project
records.organization: Catholic Charities of the Texas Panhandle
records.description_en: A free monthly supply of groceries that you pick yourself.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people age 50 or older, or people on disability.
documents_needed: Proof of address (utility bill or lease)
records.how_to_apply: Come during open hours with your documents.

records.name: Immigration Legal Services
records.organization: Catholic Charities of the Texas Panhandle
records.description_en: Low-cost help with citizenship, green cards, DACA, work permits, and other immigration papers.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For immigrants in the Texas Panhandle who need help with immigration forms.
records.how_to_apply: Call to schedule a consultation.

records.name: Utility Assistance Program (CEAP)
records.description_en: Helps pay utility bills to stop or prevent a shutoff, and teaches ways to save energy.
records.eligibility_summary_en: You must have a current utility bill, live at the home, and have income at or below 150% of the poverty guidelines.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the PCS portal. Elderly or disabled people can get a paper application at a PCS office.
records.notes: Processing can take up to 90 days. Toll-free (800) 676-4727. City of Amarillo lists (806) 373-8389 for PCS utility help. PCS serves 26 Panhandle counties including Potter and Randall.

records.name: Housing Choice Voucher Program (Panhandle)
records.description_en: Helps low-income families pay rent in a private home they choose.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income households in the 26 Panhandle counties PCS serves.
records.how_to_apply: Join the waiting list online at waitlistcheck.com or apply through the PCS portal.
records.notes: People living inside Amarillo city limits may instead use the City of Amarillo HCV program. Processing may take 30+ days.

records.name: Panhandle Transit
records.description_en: Public van rides you book ahead across the Texas Panhandle, including trips to appointments.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the public in the counties served.
records.how_to_apply: Call at least 24 hours ahead to schedule a ride.
records.notes: Demand-response service in 26 counties including Potter and Randall. Rides are based on availability.

records.name: City of Amarillo Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Program
records.description_en: Helps very low-income families pay rent for a home inside Amarillo city limits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Income limits range from $28,600 for 1 person to $53,950 for 8 people.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Housing must be within Amarillo city limits

records.how_to_apply: Apply online only through the City of Amarillo HCV portal (email needed). Free help sessions Mon, Wed, Fri 10am-1pm at 808 S Buchanan St.
records.notes: Waitlist listed as OPEN when checked.

records.name: Community Development Rent and Homeless Assistance
records.description_en: The city offers rent help and help for people who are homeless. Ask for a Housing Navigator.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Amarillo residents who are homeless or need help with rent.
records.how_to_apply: Call and ask for a Housing Navigator, or visit the office.
records.notes: Eligibility for rent help not listed; call first.

records.name: Coming Home Outreach and Supportive Housing
records.description_en: Outreach workers help people who are homeless find housing, with case management and mental health support.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people who are unsheltered, chronically homeless, or living in a shelter, especially those facing mental illness, substance use, or justice involvement.
records.how_to_apply: Fill out the Request Help form online or call.

records.name: Faith City Mission Shelter
records.description_en: Overnight shelter for men and for women with children, plus day shelter, meals, and clothing.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Amarillo who are homeless. Separate shelters for men and for women and children.
records.how_to_apply: Go to the mission during open hours.
records.hours: Day shelter Mon-Sat 7:00am-5:00pm; night shelter daily 4:30pm-7:30am
records.notes: Hours from City of Amarillo I Need Help page (https://www.amarillo.gov/community-development/i-need-help/).

records.name: Guyon Saunders Resource Center
records.description_en: A low-barrier day shelter in Amarillo for people experiencing homelessness.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people who are homeless in Amarillo.
records.how_to_apply: Walk in during open hours.
records.notes: Listed by the City of Amarillo; address and phone not confirmed this session.

records.name: The Salvation Army Amarillo Night Shelter
records.description_en: Overnight shelter in Amarillo.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Amarillo who need a place to sleep.
records.how_to_apply: Go to the shelter during evening intake hours.
records.notes: Shelter hours from the City of Amarillo I Need Help page. Local phone not listed; 1-800-SAL-ARMY is the national line.

records.name: Texas Panhandle Centers (Local Mental Health Authority)
records.description_en: The public mental health center for the Panhandle. Offers crisis help, counseling, medicine, substance use treatment, and disability services.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in the upper 21 Panhandle counties with mental health, substance use, or developmental disability needs. Anyone in crisis can call.
records.how_to_apply: In a crisis call (806) 359-6699 or 988. For services call (806) 337-1000.
records.notes: Crisis toll-free 1-800-692-4039. Adult outpatient clinic: 6600 Killgore Dr. Homeless Services: 723 N. Taylor, (806) 371-7716. Early Childhood Intervention: (806) 358-8974.

records.name: Workforce Solutions Panhandle - Amarillo Center
records.description_en: Free job search help, job training, and workshops.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to job seekers in the Texas Panhandle.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the Amarillo Center or call.

records.name: Child Care Services (CCS) - Panhandle
records.description_en: Helps working families and students pay for child care.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Income at or below 85% of state median income. Single parents need about 25 hours a week of work or school (50 combined for two parents). Child must be under 13 (under 19 with a disability).
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Texas Workforce Commission child care portal.
records.notes: Has a waitlist; non-priority families usually wait 6-9 months. Email ccapps@wspanhandle.com.

records.name: Amarillo City Transit Reduced Fare
records.description_en: Seniors, students, and people with disabilities pay half price on city buses.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For seniors, students, and people with disabilities.
documents_needed: Disability: Social Security award letter or Medicare card
records.how_to_apply: Bring your documents to the transit office during business hours to get a Reduced Fare ID card.
records.notes: Second office: 801 SE 23rd Ave. Works for single rides, day passes, and monthly passes.

records.name: ACT-Connect Paratransit
records.description_en: Door-to-door rides for people with disabilities who cannot use regular city buses.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For certified people who cannot use fixed-route buses because of a disability.
records.how_to_apply: Complete the application and physician form, then call to schedule an interview.
records.cost: $2 per trip in service area; $4 outside; free age 5 and under

records.name: Panhandle Area Agency on Aging
records.description_en: Helps older adults with meals, free rides, Medicare counseling, caregiver support, and short-term in-home help after a hospital stay.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people age 60 and older and their caregivers.
records.how_to_apply: Call the Area Agency on Aging.
records.notes: Toll-free (800) 642-6008. PRPC serves a 26-county Panhandle area.

records.name: Free Civil Legal Aid
records.description_en: Free lawyers for low-income people with civil problems like evictions, family law, and benefits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people with low income, including people on SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, WIC, or public housing. Must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, with some exceptions.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online or call the intake line. For landlord-tenant problems call (855) 548-8457.
records.notes: Serves 114 counties in North and West Texas; the county list and local Lubbock/Amarillo office addresses were not confirmed this session. No criminal or personal injury cases.
